description: Read one set by id or printed name: its series, release date, platform and card counts, with a page of its cards in printed order as checklist lines of `id`, `localId`, `name` and `rarity`. Call get_card for a card that matters. Legality is per card, from get_card: upstream's set-level flag is wrong for every current set.

language.description: Catalogue language. Names, values and set lists are localised (the Asian catalogues have their own set ids), so look values up in it; prices are the same in every language.

page.description: Zero-indexed page. A page past the end is an empty success with `hasMore` false.

set.description: The set to read, as id ('sv04.5') or printed name ('Paldean Fates'), ignoring case; a name several sets share covers them all. list_sets lists both.

size.description: Results per page; only `hasMore` says whether more exist.

name: get_set

cards.description: One page of the set's cards, in printed order, in the requested language. Four sets in the English catalogue hold no cards at all, so an empty list here is an honest answer rather than a failure. Each entry is a checklist line rather than a card record: call get_card with its id for the whole card.

id.description: The card's globally unique id, which get_card's 'id' form takes, e.g. 'sv04.5-105'.

localId.description: The number printed on the card face, which together with this set is the other way get_card finds a card. A string rather than a number because some cards are numbered with letters or symbols.

name.description: The card's printed name in the requested language.

anyOf.description: A rarity as the catalogue spells it.
The card was printed with no rarity symbol, which the catalogue spells 'None'.

rarity.description: The print rarity as the catalogue spells it. Names vary across eras, so two similarly scarce cards may not share one. Null for a card printed with no rarity symbol, such as a promo or a starter-deck card: the catalogue's own value for that is 'None', which is what the rarity filter takes to find them. Absent when the catalogue records no rarity at all — over half of Traditional Chinese cards — so absence is not the same as null.

hasMore.description: True when at least one further page of results exists after this one. Request every result by incrementing 'page' until this is false. There is deliberately no total count: the length of the returned array is the size of this page.

language.description: The catalogue language this response was read in.

page.description: The zero-indexed page of results this response holds, whether it was requested or defaulted to.

set.description: What the set is: its identity, its series, when it was released and how large it is. Tournament legality is not given for a set, because it belongs to each card — one set can mix regulation marks, and upstream's set-level flag reports every set, current ones included, as not standard-legal. Read a card's `legal` from get_card, or from search_cards at its `full` detail level.

cardCount.description: How large the set is, counted both by numbering and by printing. The printing counts are what a collector tracking a complete set has to reconcile against: a set of 'total' cards can hold far more than 'total' distinct printings.

firstEd.description: How many of them exist as a first-edition printing. Zero for every set after the early era.

holo.description: How many of them exist as a holo printing, where the artwork itself is foiled.

normal.description: How many of them exist as a non-foil printing.

official.description: How many cards are numbered in the set's printed run, which is the highest ordinary 'localId' to expect.

reverse.description: How many of them exist as a reverse-holo printing, where the card body is foiled rather than the artwork.

total.description: How many cards the set holds in total, including secret rares numbered beyond the official count.

id.description: The set's id, which is the value search_cards' 'set' filter takes, e.g. 'sv04.5'.

name.description: The set's printed name in the requested language, e.g. 'Paldean Fates'.

platform.description: Whether the set was physically printed as part of the Trading Card Game, or exists only in the digital game Pokémon TCG Pocket. Cards in a Pocket set carry no regulation mark and no tournament legality, because the Trading Card Game's formats do not apply to them.

releaseDate.description: The date the set was released, as 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

serie.description: The series this set belongs to, which is what groups sets into an era.

name.description: The series' printed name, e.g. 'Scarlet & Violet'.

size.description: The page size this response was built with, whether it was requested or defaulted to. It is the maximum number of results this page can hold, not the number it does hold — the last page holds fewer.
